analyses.name: Illumina, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The highest-scoring setup in the universe and it is breaking out today, not sitting extended - a new 52-week high on 2.23x volume with RSI at only 64.4, powered by a Q2 beat and a guidance raise.

financials.summary: Illumina is the dominant supplier of DNA sequencing instruments and, more importantly, the consumables that run on them - a razor-and-blade model where the installed base of NovaSeq and MiSeq systems generates recurring reagent and flow-cell revenue for years after the box is sold. FY2025 was the year the business stabilised after a difficult stretch: the GRAIL separation removed a large cash drain, the cost structure was reset, and instrument placements resumed growing as academic and pharma budgets normalised. The income statement still reflects that transition. Revenue returned to growth in the high single digits while reported earnings lagged - the scan's trailing figures show revenue +9.4% against EPS -9.4%, which is the signature of a company whose top line has turned before its cost base has fully worked through restructuring and amortisation. The balance sheet is the reassuring part: sequencing consumables are high-gross-margin, cash converts quickly, and the post-GRAIL company no longer funds a loss-making screening business out of the core. What changed the stock's character in the last week is the Q2 print, which beat and came with a raised full-year outlook - the market read that as confirmation that clinical volumes, not just research budgets, are now driving the consumable line.
highlights: Revenue +9.4% YoY - the return to growth after the post-pandemic sequencing downturn
EPS -9.4% YoY - reported earnings still absorbing restructuring and the GRAIL separation
Q2 2026 beat with a raised full-year guide - the specific catalyst behind the current breakout
Consumables and services now dominate the mix, giving recurring, high-gross-margin revenue
Forward P/E 33.8 - the market is paying for the clinical-volume inflection, not the trailing numbers

accomplishments: Completed the GRAIL separation, removing a large recurring cash drain from the core business
Executed a multi-phase cost-reduction programme that restored operating leverage without cutting R&D to the bone
Beat Q2 2026 estimates and raised full-year guidance, citing clinical strength and platform expansion
Broadened the NovaSeq X installed base, which is the engine for the next several years of consumable pull-through
Grew clinical and applied-market revenue faster than the research segment, reducing dependence on academic budgets

journey_52w.summary: A 125% round trip from left-for-dead to sector leader. Illumina bottomed at 91.00 within the last 52 weeks - a level that priced in permanent share loss to lower-cost sequencing competitors and a broken capital-allocation record. From there the story changed on execution rather than hype: the GRAIL overhang went away, costs came down, instrument placements resumed, and clinical volumes started carrying the consumable line. Price reclaimed its 200-DMA (now 139.69), then its 150-DMA (146.52), then built a five-contraction base above the 50-DMA. The Q2 beat and guidance raise resolved that base to the upside, and the stock is trading at 205.10 today - exactly at its 52-week high, on 2.23x average volume, with the relative-strength line at new highs. It is one of very few names to make a new high in healthcare while the technology complex is in a 15-60% drawdown.

Forward P/E 33.8 for high-single-digit revenue growth; one sell-side note already argues the stock is roughly 19% overvalued after the print
Competitive pressure on sequencing cost-per-genome from Ultima, Roche and Chinese entrants has not gone away
9.5% short interest with 4.2 days to cover means moves in either direction get amplified
Entering at the exact 52-week high leaves no cushion if the broad tape gaps down

Expansion of clinical and applied-market volumes, especially oncology and reproductive health

watch: 205.10 must now act as support - a failed breakout back below it is the signal to step aside

critical.valuation: At 205.10 Illumina trades on 33.8x forward earnings with revenue growing +9.4% and trailing EPS still negative - expensive on the trailing numbers and reasonable only if the clinical-volume inflection continues. The bull case is that the consumable annuity re-rates toward the multiples of other recurring-revenue medtech franchises as earnings catch up to revenue; the bear case is that you are paying a growth multiple for a company that grew earnings backwards last year. The chart, the volume and TradingView's 17/2 STRONG BUY all argue the market has already decided; the fundamentals need two more quarters to prove it.

analyses.name: JP Morgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: The highest-quality large-cap base in the market - a 6-contraction VCP tightened to 3.5% with EPS +46.9% at a 14.2 forward P/E and the relative-strength line already at new highs.

financials.summary: JPMorgan is the most diversified financial institution in the world and FY2025 showed why that matters in a year when rates stayed higher than the market expected. Net interest income benefited from a steep front-to-back curve and a deposit base that reprices more slowly than the asset side, while the markets and investment-banking divisions had an exceptionally strong year as capital-markets activity reopened - debt issuance, M&A advisory and equity underwriting all recovered from depressed levels. Asset and wealth management added a stable fee stream that does not depend on the balance sheet at all. The scan's trailing figures show revenue +30.4% and EPS +46.9% year over year, with earnings growing materially faster than revenue - operating leverage from a largely fixed cost base plus a benign credit environment where reserve builds stayed modest. The balance sheet remains the strongest in the industry: capital ratios well above requirements, a fortress deposit franchise, and enough excess capital to keep buying back stock while growing the loan book. That combination - cyclical revenue upside, structural fee income, and a balance sheet that can absorb a credit cycle - is why the market is willing to bid the whole group and why JPMorgan leads it.
highlights: Revenue +30.4% YoY - net interest income plus a genuine capital-markets recovery
EPS +46.9% YoY - earnings growing more than 1.5x faster than revenue on operating leverage
Forward P/E 14.2 on a $935B market cap - a low multiple for accelerating earnings
Diversified across consumer banking, cards, markets, investment banking and wealth management
Industry-leading capital ratios support continued buybacks alongside loan growth

accomplishments: Grew earnings nearly 47% while maintaining the strongest capital position among global money-centre banks
Captured outsized share in the 2025-26 capital-markets recovery across debt, equity and advisory
Expanded asset and wealth management fee income, reducing dependence on the rate cycle
Held credit costs in check through a period of rising consumer-delinquency headlines across the industry
Continued large-scale share repurchases without compromising regulatory capital

journey_52w.summary: A grinding, low-drama advance from 280.14 to 351.79 - up roughly 26% - that has never broken its 50-DMA. The path was set by rates: as it became clear the Fed would hold rather than cut aggressively, and as long-end Treasury yields kept climbing, the 8-14x financials went from value traps to the market's preferred destination. JPMorgan led that rotation rather than following it, and the relative-strength line is now at new highs even as the S&P's technology leadership has fractured. The last four months built an unusually disciplined six-contraction base that has tightened to 3.5%, with price now 1.5% below the 357.31 high and RSI at a healthy 64.7. Notably, volume has been light (0.70x) inside the base - the pattern of a stock being accumulated quietly rather than chased.

critical.valuation: 14.2x forward earnings for a franchise growing EPS at 46.9% is the cheapest growth on this list, and that gap is the entire investment case - the multiple prices in a rate-cut cycle that has not arrived. The risk is symmetric and obvious: the same 14x that looks cheap against 47% growth looks fair against the mid-single-digit growth JPMorgan would post if the curve flattened. Own it as the highest-quality expression of the rotation, size it as a core holding, and use the 50-DMA rather than a percentage as the risk reference.

analyses.name: Reliance, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cleanest industrial-materials leader in the scan - EPS +42.3% on revenue +26.5% at 17.6x forward, RS line at new highs, RSI only 62.9, and TradingView independently at STRONG BUY.

financials.summary: Reliance is North America's largest metals service centre - it buys carbon steel, aluminium, stainless and alloy from the mills, processes it to customer specification, and delivers small quantities fast to tens of thousands of industrial customers. The critical thing to understand about the model is that Reliance is not a commodity producer: it earns a spread between the mill price and the delivered price, and that spread is widest when metal prices are rising and most defensible when volumes are steady. Roughly half of orders ship same-day or next-day, which is a service business the mills cannot replicate and importers cannot match. FY2025 showed the model working at both ends. Revenue grew +26.5% on a combination of higher metal pricing and genuine volume growth from reshoring-driven industrial construction, data-centre buildout and defence-related fabrication. Earnings grew faster still at +42.3% - the operating leverage of a distribution network whose fixed costs are already in place. The balance sheet is conservatively run, with modest leverage and a long record of funding acquisitions of family-owned service centres out of cash flow rather than debt. That is why the stock trades at a premium to the mills: the earnings are less volatile than steel prices imply.
highlights: Revenue +26.5% YoY - both price and volume contributing, not just metal inflation
EPS +42.3% YoY - earnings growing 1.6x faster than revenue on distribution operating leverage
Forward P/E 17.6 - a premium to the mills, justified by the spread-based rather than commodity-based model
Same-day and next-day delivery on roughly half of orders - a genuine service moat
$20.7B market cap with conservative leverage and a long acquisition track record funded from cash flow

accomplishments: Grew earnings 42% in a year when steel prices themselves were far less directional than the earnings line
Continued the roll-up of family-owned regional service centres, adding capacity without balance-sheet strain
Captured reshoring and data-centre construction demand, which required no new capacity to serve
Maintained gross margins through metal-price volatility, demonstrating the spread model works in both directions
Reached a 52-week high of 414.33 with the relative-strength line at new highs versus the S&P 500

journey_52w.summary: A 55% advance from 262.77 to 406.10 driven by exactly the thing that is now leading the whole market - the industrial rotation. Reliance spent the first part of the last year discounted as a cyclical whose earnings were assumed to be peaking; instead volumes held and spreads widened as reshoring capex, grid investment and data-centre construction all arrived at once. Price worked steadily above its 200-DMA (328.86), then its 150-DMA (346.11), and the last three months have been a tight three-contraction base squeezing to 3.2% above a rising 390.41 50-DMA. The relative-strength line is at new highs and four-week relative strength is +8.2%, so this is active leadership, not drift. At 406.10 the stock is 2.0% under its high with RSI at only 62.9 - the un-extended half of the steel trade, in contrast to Nucor at RSI 71.1.

risks: Basic materials is cyclical - a growth scare hits this before it hits staples or utilities
Steel and aluminium pricing is the swing factor on spreads and it is outside management's control
Tariff and trade-policy changes cut both ways for a domestic distributor of imported and domestic metal
$20.7B market cap means thinner liquidity than the mega-cap leaders in this list
Already 55% above the 262.77 low - this is a continuation entry, not a bottom
catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings on 22 October
Continued reshoring, grid and data-centre construction awards feeding volume
Any acceleration in domestic steel pricing, which widens the spread directly
Further tuck-in acquisitions of regional service centres
watch: 414.33 is the breakout trigger
390.41 is the 50-DMA; the base fails below roughly 373
Domestic hot-rolled coil pricing as the leading indicator for the spread

critical.valuation: 17.6x forward earnings with EPS growing 42.3% is a reasonable price for a business whose earnings are structurally less volatile than the steel price. Against the mills, Reliance deserves and gets a premium - it has no blast-furnace fixed costs and no commodity exposure it cannot pass through. The honest caveat is cycle position: this is the fourth or fifth inning of an industrial capex upturn, not the first, so the multiple is being paid on earnings that are already well above trend. Own it as the highest-quality materials exposure, keep the stop at the 50-DMA, and take the RS-line-at-new-highs signal as the reason it is preferable to Nucor here.

analyses.name: Valero Energy Corporation
analyses.verdict: The purest expression of an extraordinary refining margin cycle - EPS +453.5% at 11.4x forward, RS line at new highs, 0.2% from its high - with one obvious catch: Iran talks open today.

financials.summary: Valero is the largest independent refiner in the world, with a Gulf Coast-weighted system that is structurally advantaged: it can run heavy and sour crude grades that trade at a discount, it has direct access to export markets, and it does not carry the upstream exposure that makes the integrated majors a bet on crude price rather than on margin. Refining is a spread business - the crack spread between crude input and refined product output - and FY2025 into 2026 has produced one of the widest spread environments in the industry's history. The cause is supply-side: Middle East disruption around the Strait of Hormuz constrained product flows, global refining capacity has been retired faster than it has been added, and demand for diesel and jet fuel held firm. The result on the income statement is dramatic - revenue +51.7% and EPS +453.5% year over year, because refining earnings are levered: a modest widening of the crack spread multiplies straight through to net income on an essentially fixed cost base. Valero also has a renewable diesel and ethanol segment that adds a secondary, policy-driven earnings stream. The balance sheet was repaired during the good years, so the company enters this period with low net debt and has been returning the windfall through buybacks and dividends rather than expanding capacity into the top of the cycle - which is the right capital-allocation instinct and part of why the multiple has not collapsed.
highlights: Revenue +51.7% YoY on higher refined-product realisations and firm throughput
EPS +453.5% YoY - the operating leverage of a spread business on a fixed cost base
Forward P/E 11.4 - the market is explicitly pricing these earnings as unsustainable
Gulf Coast system runs discounted heavy/sour grades with direct export access
Windfall returned via buybacks and dividends rather than capacity expansion at the cycle top

accomplishments: Grew earnings more than fivefold as the crack spread widened, without adding capacity or leverage
Ran high utilisation through a period of severe global product-flow disruption
Returned the bulk of the margin windfall to shareholders through buybacks rather than reinvesting at peak economics
Maintained a low net-debt position, leaving the company able to absorb a normalisation in spreads
Reached a 52-week high of 313.59 with the relative-strength line at new highs and +16.9% four-week relative strength

journey_52w.summary: A 142% advance from 129.03 to 312.90 - the single largest move among the large-cap leaders in this scan - and it is a geopolitics story from beginning to end. Refining margins were merely adequate a year ago. Then Middle East escalation culminated in disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, product flows were constrained, and crack spreads went vertical. Valero's earnings followed with a lag and a multiplier. Price cleared its 200-DMA (216.47), then compounded above a rising 50-DMA (269.32) in a four-contraction base tightening to 5.1%, and the relative-strength line is now at new highs with +16.9% added in the last four weeks alone. At 312.90 the stock sits 0.2% from its 52-week high with RSI at 62.6 - remarkably un-extended for a stock that has more than doubled. The reason today matters is that the same geopolitics is now reversing: Trump cancelled the planned strike on Iran to pursue a nuclear deal, talks begin today, tankers are clearing the Red Sea, and crude has slid. The chart has not broken; the catalyst is now two-way.

Refining margins mean-revert violently; Reuters is already calling this refining golden era temporary

Q3 2026 earnings on 22 October
Weekly refined-product inventory and crack-spread data
Continued buyback execution, which supports the price independent of the spread
watch: Iran headlines are the position risk, not the chart - a deal signed is a reason to cut, not to hold and hope
313.59 is the trigger, 287.87 the stop, 269.32 the 50-DMA backstop
Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread as the real-time read on earnings power
Whether MPC and PSX hold their own highs - if the refining group breaks together, exit together
critical.valuation: 11.4x forward earnings on EPS that grew 453% is the market telling you plainly that it does not believe these earnings recur - and the market is probably right about the level while being wrong about the timing. The correct way to hold Valero here is as a momentum position with an event risk you can name and date: the chart, the relative strength and the buyback all support it, and a normalisation in spreads is a question of when rather than whether. Trade it with the stop honoured and treat a genuine Iran agreement as a thesis-invalidating headline rather than a dip to buy.

analyses.name: DexCom, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A new 52-week high on 2.47x volume with RSI at only 61.6 and TradingView showing 16 buy signals against zero sells - the rare heavy-volume breakout that is not yet overbought.

financials.summary: DexCom sells continuous glucose monitoring systems - wearable sensors that transmit glucose readings to a phone or pump every few minutes, replacing fingerstick testing. The economics are a razor-and-blade annuity: the transmitter and receiver are cheap or bundled, and the recurring revenue comes from sensors that a patient replaces every ten days for life. That produces very high gross margins, extremely predictable revenue, and a customer base that essentially never churns once a physician has prescribed the system. FY2025 continued the pattern of durable double-digit revenue growth with margin expansion, and the scan's trailing figures show revenue +13.1% with EPS +43.6% - earnings growing more than three times faster than the top line, which is what happens when a high-fixed-cost manufacturing base scales into an expanding installed base. The strategically important development is the relationship with GLP-1 therapies. The initial fear was that weight-loss drugs would shrink the diabetic population and therefore the CGM market; the reality has been the opposite - GLP-1 prescribing has pulled more type-2 patients into active metabolic management, expanded reimbursement for glucose monitoring in non-insulin-using type-2 diabetes, and opened a genuine adjacent market in metabolic health for non-diabetics. The addressable market got bigger, not smaller.
highlights: Revenue +13.1% YoY from recurring ten-day sensor replacement - an annuity, not a capital-equipment cycle
EPS +43.6% YoY - earnings growing 3.3x faster than revenue on manufacturing scale
Very high gross margin on consumable sensors with essentially zero customer churn
GLP-1 adoption has expanded the addressable CGM market rather than contracting it
Forward P/E 26.8 on a $31.5B cap - a reasonable multiple for 40%+ earnings growth

accomplishments: Expanded reimbursement into non-insulin-using type-2 diabetes, which is the largest incremental patient pool
Grew earnings more than 40% while revenue grew 13% - genuine operating leverage from sensor manufacturing scale
Launched into the over-the-counter metabolic-health market, opening a non-diabetic customer base
Turned the GLP-1 narrative from an existential threat into a demand driver
Broke to a new 52-week high at 83.45 on 2.47x average volume with +36.0% three-month momentum

journey_52w.summary: A 52% advance from 54.84 to 83.45 that is really the story of a narrative being corrected. A year ago DexCom traded as a company whose end market was about to be shrunk by GLP-1 drugs, and the multiple compressed accordingly. What followed was the opposite: GLP-1 prescribing expanded metabolic-health engagement, reimbursement widened into type-2 patients who do not use insulin, and the sensor installed base grew faster than before. Price reclaimed its 200-DMA (67.75) and 150-DMA (68.97), built above a rising 50-DMA at 73.13 through a six-contraction consolidation - loose by leadership standards, with a 9.6% tightest pullback - and broke to a new high at 83.45 today on 2.47x average volume with +36.0% three-month momentum. RSI at 61.6 on a breakout day is unusual and constructive: the move has room. TradingView's read is unanimous on the buy side, 16 buy signals against zero sells.

critical.valuation: At 83.45 DexCom trades on 26.8x forward earnings against 43.6% EPS growth and 13.1% revenue growth - a PEG well under 1 on earnings, which is unusual for a medtech franchise with this much revenue visibility. The multiple is defensible because the revenue is recurring and the gross margin is structurally high; the risk is that 40%+ earnings growth is a scaling phenomenon that decays as the installed base matures, at which point 26.8x on 13% revenue growth looks full. The immediate case is technical and strong: a new high on 2.47x volume with RSI at 61.6 and zero sell signals from TradingView is about as clean a breakout as this scan produced today.

analyses.name: NetApp, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The only large technology name with its relative-strength line at new highs while QQQ trades below its 50-DMA - and it costs 18.1x forward earnings.

financials.summary: NetApp sells enterprise data storage - all-flash arrays, hybrid-cloud storage operating systems, and the software layer that lets the same data management work on-premises and inside AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. The business has two characteristics that matter right now. First, it is genuinely AI-adjacent without being AI-dependent: training and inference workloads need high-throughput storage next to the GPUs, and NetApp's all-flash portfolio has been the beneficiary, but the majority of revenue is still ordinary enterprise refresh and cloud-storage subscription that would continue with or without the AI capex cycle. Second, the mix has been shifting toward software and support - recurring, high-margin revenue that now underpins the earnings base. FY2026 showed both: revenue +12.5% with EPS +23.4%, so earnings grew roughly twice as fast as the top line, driven by all-flash share gains, a richer software mix and disciplined operating expense. Gross margins are well above the hardware-vendor average because so much of the value sits in ONTAP software rather than the enclosure. The balance sheet is clean and the company has consistently returned cash through buybacks and a dividend. What the market has not done is pay for any of it - at 18.1x forward earnings NetApp trades at roughly a third of Fortinet's multiple and a fifth of Snowflake's, which is the entire point of owning it here.
highlights: Revenue +12.5% YoY with EPS +23.4% - earnings growing about 2x the top line on mix shift
Forward P/E 18.1 - the cheapest AI-adjacent multiple in the technology group
All-flash array share gains plus a growing recurring software and support base
Hybrid-cloud storage software runs natively inside all three major public clouds
$35B market cap with consistent buybacks and a dividend - capital return, not capital consumption

accomplishments: Grew earnings 23% in a fiscal year when most storage and enterprise-hardware peers saw multiple compression
Won all-flash share against Pure Storage and Dell as AI workloads pulled forward storage refresh cycles
Established first-party hybrid-cloud storage services inside AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
Shifted the revenue mix toward recurring software and support, lifting structural gross margin

journey_52w.summary: A 91% advance from 93.35 to 178.50 that stands almost alone in technology. NetApp began the period valued as a legacy storage vendor in secular decline. analyses.name: Prologis, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The world's largest industrial landlord resting exactly on its 50-DMA with EPS +85.3% and RSI 54.8 - a defined-risk entry, with TradingView neutral and no momentum confirmation.

financials.summary: Prologis owns and develops logistics real estate - distribution warehouses and fulfilment centres - at genuine global scale, with a portfolio spanning the Americas, Europe and Asia. The economics of the business right now are almost entirely about re-leasing spreads. Leases signed five to ten years ago are expiring at rents far below current market, and each renewal resets to today's level, which drops almost entirely to the bottom line because the asset is already built and the operating cost is largely passed through. That is why FY2025 shows revenue +12.3% but EPS +85.3% - earnings growing roughly seven times faster than revenue. The second engine is development: Prologis has a large land bank in supply-constrained submarkets and earns a development margin on top of the rental yield, plus a growing data-centre conversion pipeline on power-adjacent industrial sites that is becoming a genuine secondary story. The complication in the sector is supply. A large national wave of speculative warehouse construction was delivered into 2024-25, and vacancy in Sun Belt and secondary markets is still being absorbed. Prologis is comparatively insulated because its portfolio is weighted to coastal, infill, port-adjacent locations where new supply is physically hard to add - but it is not immune, and market rent growth has decelerated from the extraordinary 2022-23 pace.

analyses.name: Liquidia Corporation
analyses.verdict: The highest-momentum name in the scan with an actual commercial engine behind it - +120.5% in three months on the Yutrepia launch - and an earnings print nine days out that will decide the next leg.

financials.summary: Liquidia is a single-product commercial-stage pharmaceutical company. Yutrepia is a dry-powder inhaled formulation of treprostinil for pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease - a market where the incumbent, United Therapeutics' Tyvaso, has generated billions in annual revenue. The clinical argument for Yutrepia is delivery: a dry-powder inhaler with a shorter administration time and better tolerability profile than nebulised alternatives, which matters enormously for adherence in a chronically ill patient population. The financial picture is what you would expect of a company in its first full commercial year and it needs to be read carefully. The scan shows revenue growth of +4158%, which is an arithmetic artefact of scaling off a near-zero base rather than a meaningful growth rate - the correct way to read it is that Yutrepia went from essentially no revenue to a real, measurable commercial ramp. Trailing EPS growth is not computable because the company is still loss-making: it is spending on sales force, specialty-pharmacy distribution and market access ahead of the revenue curve. That is the right thing to do in a launch year, but it means the balance sheet and the cash runway are as important as the income statement. Forward P/E of 14.5 reflects sell-side models that assume the ramp continues to scale; it is a projection, not a current earnings multiple.

analyses.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The one mega-cap that is actually working - within 1.2% of its high on 2.83x volume, the heaviest institutional footprint in the scan, with EPS +242% and zero sell signals from TradingView.

financials.summary: Amazon is three businesses that happen to share a balance sheet: a retail marketplace and logistics network, a cloud-infrastructure provider in AWS, and an advertising business that is now among the largest in the world. FY2025 was the year the operating leverage the bulls had promised for a decade finally showed up in reported numbers. Revenue grew +19.6% while EPS grew +242.3% - the gap is the whole story. Retail margins expanded as the regionalised fulfilment network matured and the cost-to-serve per unit fell; AWS re-accelerated as enterprises resumed migration spending and AI inference workloads landed on Bedrock and custom Trainium silicon; and advertising, which carries structurally higher margin than either, grew faster than the company average. The complication is capital intensity. Amazon is spending at unprecedented scale on data centres, custom AI chips and power, and the market has spent this quarter punishing capex intensity across the hyperscaler group. Amazon's defence is that its capex is demand-driven - it is building against booked AWS commitments rather than speculatively - and that the retail and advertising cash flows fund it without leverage. Free cash flow remains positive and the balance sheet carries net cash, which is why the stock has held up while ORCL, which financed its AI build differently, is 60% off its high.

analyses.name: Apple Inc.
analyses.verdict: Sitting exactly on its 50-DMA with intact fundamentals and TradingView flatly negative at 4 buy versus 13 sell - a hold on the line, not a place to add.

financials.summary: Apple's financial model is now two businesses. The hardware franchise - iPhone, Mac, iPad, Watch - generates the installed base, and the Services business monetises it through the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, advertising, payments and the Google search licensing arrangement. Services carries roughly double the gross margin of hardware, so as its share of revenue grows, blended margin expands regardless of unit volumes. FY2025 reflected that: the scan's trailing figures show revenue +16.4% with EPS +28.7%, earnings growing well ahead of the top line on mix shift plus buyback-driven share-count reduction. The balance sheet is unique in scale - enormous cash generation, a net cash position, and the largest buyback programme in corporate history, which mechanically supports EPS growth even in a flat revenue year. What the market is genuinely uncertain about is the next platform cycle. Apple's on-device AI strategy has been slower and more cautious than peers, the Siri overhaul has slipped, and the company has ceded the visible AI narrative to Google and OpenAI while arguing that privacy-preserving on-device inference is the durable position. Meanwhile the Google search licensing payment - a very large, very high-margin Services line - is exposed to antitrust remedies. The fundamentals are intact; the narrative is contested.

analyses.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING - the quant score is noise. What is real: an all-time low at 108.37, 48.7% below the IPO high, RSI 19.2, and the first-ever public quarterly report on Wednesday.

financials.period: FY2025 (first disclosed full fiscal year; pre-IPO financials, limited public history)
financials.summary: SpaceX is two businesses bolted together. The launch business flies Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy for commercial satellite operators, NASA and national-security customers, and its structural advantage is reusability - recovering and reflying boosters gives a cost-per-kilogram to orbit that no competitor has matched, which is why SpaceX has come to dominate global launch cadence. The second and increasingly more important business is Starlink, a low-earth-orbit broadband constellation sold as a monthly consumer and enterprise subscription. Starlink converts SpaceX from a lumpy, contract-driven launch provider into a recurring-revenue communications utility, and it is the reason the IPO commanded the valuation it did. The financial disclosure available publicly is thin - this is a company that listed only weeks ago and has not yet reported as a public entity. The scan shows revenue growth of +15.4% and a forward P/E of 120, which together are the entire problem: a $1.43 trillion market cap on mid-teens revenue growth and triple-digit forward earnings is a price set for flawless execution over a decade. Starship, the fully reusable heavy-lift vehicle, is the option that justified that framing - lunar and Mars architecture, national-security heavy lift, and a step-change in launch economics - but it is an option, not current cash flow. Wednesday 5 August is the first quarter this company has ever reported to public shareholders, and it will establish the first real anchor for all of these numbers.

critical.valuation: Any valuation statement here is provisional: mid-teens revenue growth against a $1.43T market cap and a ~120x forward multiple is an extraordinary price, and a 48.7% decline from the IPO high has corrected some of that without making it obviously cheap. The business case is genuinely strong - Starlink is a real recurring-revenue utility, Falcon 9 reusability is a durable cost moat, and Starship is a large option. The listing price simply did not leave room for any of it to be discovered. For holders, the honest position is that this is now a business-quality bet with no technical support underneath it, and Wednesday's report is the first opportunity to replace speculation with numbers.

analyses.name: Fortinet, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Cybersecurity has decoupled from the rest of tech - +87.7% three-month momentum fully digested down to an RSI of 51.7, with TradingView's strongest technology read at 17 buy / 1 sell.

financials.summary: Fortinet sells network security - firewalls, secure SD-WAN, and an integrated security platform - and its structural differentiator is silicon. Fortinet designs its own ASICs for security processing, which gives it a materially better performance-per-dollar and performance-per-watt profile than competitors running on general-purpose CPUs. That translates directly into the best operating margins in the security industry and into pricing flexibility that Palo Alto and Check Point cannot easily match. The revenue model has been shifting from appliance sales toward subscription services - FortiGuard threat intelligence, SASE and cloud security - which raises recurring revenue and gross margin at the same time. FY2025 delivered revenue +25.6% with EPS +43.9%, so earnings grew roughly 1.7x faster than revenue on the combination of subscription mix shift and the ASIC cost advantage. Fortinet also converts revenue to cash unusually well because customers pay for multi-year service contracts upfront, generating substantial deferred revenue and a balance sheet with meaningful net cash. The strategic question is the same one facing the whole group: whether platform consolidation favours Palo Alto's breadth or Fortinet's price-performance, and whether Microsoft's bundled security offerings compress the market from below. So far Fortinet's numbers say it is winning on the mid-market and service-provider end while holding enterprise share.
highlights: Revenue +25.6% YoY with EPS +43.9% - subscription mix shift plus the ASIC cost advantage

Delivered +87.7% three-month momentum and then held it - price is within 2.9% of the high with RSI at only 51.7

journey_52w.summary: A 118% advance from 74.39 to 161.95 that has almost nothing to do with the rest of technology. Fortinet spent the early part of the period recovering from a firewall-refresh air pocket that had crushed the multiple. As the refresh cycle resumed and the subscription mix kept lifting margin, earnings re-accelerated and the stock re-rated hard - clearing the 200-DMA (100.54) and 150-DMA (106.48) and compounding above a rising 50-DMA at 149.67. What makes the current setup unusual is the digestion: after +87.7% in three months, RSI has come all the way back to 51.7 while price stayed within 2.9% of the 166.83 high. That is a stock consolidating gains, not stalling. The relative-strength line is at new highs, and security has visibly decoupled from AI infrastructure - Fortinet is up while ORCL is 60% off its high and VRT is 36% off. The one soft spot is that four-week relative strength has flattened to +0.3%, so the leadership is currently pausing. Earnings are already behind it. TradingView rates it STRONG BUY 17 buy / 1 sell - the strongest technical confirmation of any technology name in the scan.

critical.valuation: 43.2x forward earnings against 43.9% EPS growth is roughly a PEG of 1 - fully valued rather than cheap, and the whole case rests on the growth persisting. What justifies paying it here is the combination of structurally superior margins from the ASIC architecture, a revenue mix moving toward recurring subscriptions, and the fact that security budgets are the last line item enterprises cut - which is exactly the characteristic you want in a bifurcated tape. TradingView's 17/1 STRONG BUY is the strongest technical confirmation available in technology today, and RSI at 51.7 after an 88% run means you are not paying for the momentum you are inheriting.
